newsitem.title: SPAIN: SWIMMING-POPOV LOOKING FORWARD TO EUROPEAN TEST.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-POPOV LOOKING FORWARD TO EUROPEAN TEST.

text.p: Alexander Popov, knifed in the abdomen last year, is confident his powers are undiminished as he faces his first major championships since his double Olympic triumph in Atlanta.

The 25-year-old Russian swims this week in the European championships, the competition in which he gained his first taste of the international limelight when he won the 100 metres freestyle title in Athens in 1991.

Popov has been based in Australia for the past four years but has always returned to excel at the European championships, where he followed his 1991 win with 50 and 100 metres freestyle title doubles in 1993 and 1995.

"I'm really happy to be in Europe...the continent where I won my first gold medal," said Popov, who has achieved global doubles in the same events at the 1992 and 1996 Olympics and 1994 world championships.
"This competition is very important to me. It's the biggest event before the world championships (next January in Perth, Australia). I hope this competition will help me get back to where I was."

Popov, fully recovered after being stabbed by a melon-seller in a Moscow street last August, is one of four Olympic champions competing in six days of racing in the San Pablo pool which begin on Tuesday.

Ireland's Michelle de Bruin, adopting her married name for the first time at a major international championships since her golden Olympic treble in Atlanta as Michelle Smith, has her name down for seven events but has had one (100 butterfly) disallowed because it was added to the others too late.
She may not swim all the six other races but has every chance of matching or even surpassing the four individual golds achieved by Hungary's Krisztina Egerszegi in 1993.
De Bruin enters the fray on Tuesday in the 400 individual medley, one of the three events -- along with the 400 freestyle and 200 individual medley -- she won at the 1996 Olympics.

She tasted her first major international long-course success when she won the 200 butterfly and 200 individual medley at the last European championships in Vienna in 1995 at the advanced age of 25, having made controversially monumental progress after years as an also-ran.

Fellow Olympic champions Denis Pankratov of Russia (100 and 200 butterfly) and Frederik DeBurghgraeve of Belgium (100 breaststroke) are world record holders in their events and it would be a surprise if they failed to retain their European crowns.

Three Hungarian Olympic gold medallists are absent -- Egerszegi, who has retired, and Norbert Rosza (200 breaststroke) and Attila Czene (200 medley), who are staying away because it is too close to next January's world championships for their Perth preparations.
For Popov, by contrast, the European event will be a good test. "If there are any mistakes we'll try to resolve them before the world championships in Perth," he said.
He feels he has not raced enough to set new world standards but is optimistic for the future.
"I can't promise I'll do a world record here but it might be coming, who knows?" he said. "We'll produce a couple of good times here."
Popov is not the fastest man in Europe this year in either the 50 or 100 freestyle but nobody can match his pedigree.
"The biggest challenger for me will be myself. I'll try to get back to where I was last year and the year before," he said.
And rivals should beware because the master stylist says he has been working a lot to improve his technique.
"I've felt smoother this year. It takes less energy to swim the same times as last year," he said.
